instruction:
Write a `Dockerfile` for a Node.js 20 web service. Source layout: `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `server.js`, `src/`.
Requirements: use a pinned Alpine-based Node 20 image (not :latest), work in /app, install only production dependencies
reproducibly from the lockfile, make sure editing source code does not invalidate the dependency-install layer, run as the
unprivileged `node` user, document port 3000, and start with `node server.js` in exec form.

reference.Dockerfile:
FROM node:20-alpine3.19
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev
COPY . .
USER node
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "server.js"]

instruction:
Write a `Dockerfile` for a Flask app (`app.py` exposing `app`, plus `requirements.txt`). Use `python:3.12-slim` pinned to a
minor version tag, keep pip from leaving its cache in the image, copy requirements first for layer caching, create and switch
to a dedicated non-root user, expose 8000, add a HEALTHCHECK that works WITHOUT curl installed (python stdlib is fine), and
run `gunicorn -b 0.0.0.0:8000 app:app` in exec form.

FROM python:3.12.4-slim
ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
WORKDIR /srv
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
RUN useradd --system --uid 10001 --no-create-home appuser
USER appuser
EXPOSE 8000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --retries=3 CMD ["python", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/')"]
CMD ["gunicorn", "-b", "0.0.0.0:8000", "app:app"]

must be compiled in a layer that only invalidates when Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock change. Use the dummy-main trick (copy the manifests, create a
stub `src/main.rs` containing `fn main() {}`, run `cargo build --release --locked`, then copy the real sources and build again).
Multi-stage: builder `rust:1.79-slim-bookworm` (pinned), runtime `debian:bookworm-slim` (pinned) containing only the binary

COPY src ./src
RUN touch src/main.rs && cargo build --release --locked

RUN useradd --system --uid 10001 app
COPY --from=builder /app/target/release/app /usr/local/bin/app
USER app
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/app"]

Keep the same runtime result: Debian packages installed (with proper apt hygiene), the app under /opt/reports, the `reports` user (no root at runtime),

apt-get install -y python3 python3-pip ca-certificates

chown -R reports:reports /var/reports

`RollingUpdate` with `maxUnavailable: 0` and `maxSurge: 1`, `minReadySeconds: 10`, a startupProbe (GET /healthz, failureThreshold 30, periodSeconds 2), readinessProbe (GET /ready), livenessProbe (GET /healthz),
a `preStop` exec hook `sleep 10` so endpoints drain before SIGTERM, `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45`, and a `topologySpreadConstraints` entry spreading pods over `kubernetes.io/hostname` (maxSkew 1, `whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway`)

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: checkout
  labels:
    app: checkout
spec:
  replicas: 4
  minReadySeconds: 10
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0
      maxSurge: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: checkout
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: checkout
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45
      topologySpreadConstraints:
        - maxSkew: 1
          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
          whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
          labelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: checkout
      containers:
        - name: checkout
          image: ghcr.io/acme/checkout:6.0.1
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
          startupProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: http
            failureThreshold: 30
            periodSeconds: 2
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 5
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 10
          lifecycle:
            preStop:
              exec:
                command: ["sleep", "10"]
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 200m
              memory: 256Mi
            limits:
              memory: 512Mi

instruction:
Write `.gitlab-ci.yml` for a Node project with stages `build`, `test`, `deploy`. Default image `node:20.14-alpine` (pinned). Cache `node_modules/` keyed on the lockfile
(`cache.key.files: [package-lock.json]`, policy pull-push). Job `build`: `npm ci` and `npm run build`, artifacts `dist/` expiring in 1 week. Job `test` (stage test): `npm test`, needs build, with `coverage` regex and junit report artifact
(`reports.junit: junit.xml`). Job `deploy` (stage deploy): runs `./deploy.sh` only on the default branch (use `rules`, not `only`), `when: manual`, in environment `production`. `interruptible: true` on build and test.

stages: [build, test, deploy]
default:
  image: node:20.14-alpine
  cache:
    key:
      files:
        - package-lock.json
    paths:
      - node_modules/
    policy: pull-push
build:
  stage: build
  interruptible: true
  script:
    - npm ci
    - npm run build
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - dist/
    expire_in: 1 week
test:
  stage: test
  interruptible: true
  needs: [build]
  script:
    - npm test
  coverage: '/All files[^|]*\|[^|]*\s+([\d\.]+)/'
  artifacts:
    when: always
    reports:
      junit: junit.xml
deploy:
  stage: deploy
  script:
    - ./deploy.sh
  environment:
    name: production
  rules:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
      when: manual

instruction:
Write `.github/workflows/release.yml` triggered on tags `v*`. Job `build` (read-only token) builds with `make dist`, uploads `dist/` as artifact `dist` (`actions/upload-artifact@v4`, retention 7 days).
Job `publish` (`needs: build`) downloads it (`actions/download-artifact@v4`) and creates a GitHub release from the tag with `softprops/action-gh-release@c95fe1489396fe8a9eb87c0abf8aa5b2ef267fda` attaching `dist/*`.
Only `publish` gets `contents: write`; top-level permissions are `contents: read`.

name: release
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: make dist
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: dist
          path: dist/
          retention-days: 7
  publish:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: dist
          path: dist/
      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@c95fe1489396fe8a9eb87c0abf8aa5b2ef267fda
        with:
          files: dist/*

Write `check_env.sh` (bash, `set -euo pipefail` style safe even when variables are unset). `check_env.sh VAR1 VAR2 ...` verifies that every named environment variable is set AND non-empty.
If all are fine print `all set` and exit 0. Otherwise print `missing: ` followed by the missing names (in argument order, space separated) to STDERR and exit 1. With no arguments it prints `all set`.

reference.check_env.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

missing=()
for name in "$@"; do
  if [ -z "${!name:-}" ]; then
    missing+=("$name")
  fi
done

if [ "${#missing[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "missing: ${missing[*]}" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "all set"

instruction:
Write `retry.sh` (bash): `retry.sh ATTEMPTS DELAY command [args...]` runs the command up to ATTEMPTS times (ATTEMPTS must be a positive integer). Stop at the first success and exit 0.
After each failed attempt print `attempt <i>/<ATTEMPTS> failed (rc=<code>)` to stderr and, if more attempts remain, `sleep DELAY` (use the `sleep` command so it can be stubbed; never sleep after the last attempt).
If all attempts fail, exit with the exit code of the last attempt. Wrong usage (fewer than 3 args or non-numeric ATTEMPTS): message to stderr, exit 2. The command's arguments must be passed through exactly (quoting preserved). Shellcheck-clean.

reference.retry.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail

if [ $# -lt 3 ]; then
  echo "usage: $0 ATTEMPTS DELAY command [args...]" >&2
  exit 2
fi
attempts=$1
delay=$2
shift 2
case $attempts in
  '' | *[!0-9]* | 0) echo "ATTEMPTS must be a positive integer" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

rc=0
for ((i = 1; i <= attempts; i++)); do
  if "$@"; then
    exit 0
  else
    rc=$?
  fi
  echo "attempt $i/$attempts failed (rc=$rc)" >&2
  if [ "$i" -lt "$attempts" ]; then
    sleep "$delay"
  fi
done
exit "$rc"

Write `wait_for.sh` (bash): `wait_for.sh HOST PORT TIMEOUT` waits until `nc -z HOST PORT` succeeds. Poll once per second using `sleep 1`; give up after TIMEOUT seconds of waiting.
On success print `HOST:PORT is up` (stdout) and exit 0 without sleeping if the first probe already works. On timeout print `timeout waiting for HOST:PORT after TIMEOUTs` to stderr and exit 1.
Wrong usage: exit 2. Do not use `timeout`/background tricks, just a loop. Shellcheck-clean.

reference.wait_for.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

[ $# -eq 3 ] || { echo "usage: $0 HOST PORT TIMEOUT" >&2; exit 2; }
host=$1
port=$2
timeout=$3

elapsed=0
while ! nc -z "$host" "$port"; do
  if [ "$elapsed" -ge "$timeout" ]; then
    echo "timeout waiting for $host:$port after ${timeout}s" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 1
  elapsed=$((elapsed + 1))
done
echo "$host:$port is up"

instruction:
Write `cleanup.sh` (bash) that removes exited Docker containers safely. It lists them with `docker ps -aq --filter status=exited`. Default is a DRY RUN: for each container id print `would remove <id>` and call nothing else.
With `--yes` it runs `docker rm <id>` for each id (one call per id, output of docker rm suppressed) and prints `removed <id>`. If there are no exited containers print `nothing to remove`.
Any other argument: usage message on stderr and exit 2. Shellcheck-clean.

reference.cleanup.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

apply=0
case "${1:-}" in
  "") ;;
  --yes) apply=1 ;;
  *) echo "usage: $0 [--yes]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

mapfile -t ids < <(docker ps -aq --filter status=exited)
if [ "${#ids[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "nothing to remove"
  exit 0
fi

for id in "${ids[@]}"; do
  if [ "$apply" -eq 1 ]; then
    docker rm "$id" > /dev/null
    echo "removed $id"
  else
    echo "would remove $id"
  fi
done

Write `deploy.sh` (bash): `deploy.sh ENV VERSION`. ENV must be `staging` or `prod`; VERSION must look like `v1.2.3` (v + three dot-separated numbers). Anything else: usage on stderr, exit 2, no kubectl calls.

Deploy: `kubectl -n ENV set image deployment/app app=registry.example.com/app:VERSION`, then `kubectl -n ENV rollout status deployment/app --timeout=120s`.
If the rollout status command fails: print `rollout failed, rolling back` to stderr, run `kubectl -n ENV rollout undo deployment/app` and exit 1. On success print `deployed VERSION to ENV`. Shellcheck-clean.

reference.deploy.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  echo "usage: $0 staging|prod vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH" >&2
  exit 2
}

[ $# -eq 2 ] || usage
env=$1
version=$2
case $env in
  staging | prod) ;;
  *) usage ;;
esac
[[ $version =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]] || usage

if [ "$env" = prod ] && [ "${CONFIRM:-}" != yes ]; then
  echo "refusing to deploy to prod without CONFIRM=yes" >&2
  exit 3
fi

image="registry.example.com/app:$version"
kubectl -n "$env" set image deployment/app app="$image"
if ! kubectl -n "$env" rollout status deployment/app --timeout=120s; then
  echo "rollout failed, rolling back" >&2
  kubectl -n "$env" rollout undo deployment/app
  exit 1
fi
echo "deployed $version to $env"

  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 5 "$url" || true)

instruction:
Write `locked.sh` (bash): `locked.sh command [args...]` runs the command while holding a lock directory (create it atomically with `mkdir`) at `$LOCK_DIR` (default `/tmp/locked.lock`) so cron jobs never overlap.
If the lock is already held: print `already running (lock <path>)` to stderr, exit 75, and do NOT run the command and do NOT remove the other process's lock. Otherwise run the command and exit with ITS exit code.
The lock must be released (directory removed) in every case where we acquired it: success, command failure, and when the script is interrupted by SIGTERM/SIGINT (use `trap`). No arguments: usage, exit 2. Shellcheck-clean.

reference.locked.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail

[ $# -ge 1 ] || { echo "usage: $0 command [args...]" >&2; exit 2; }
lock=${LOCK_DIR:-/tmp/locked.lock}

if ! mkdir "$lock" 2> /dev/null; then
  echo "already running (lock $lock)" >&2
  exit 75
fi
trap 'rmdir "$lock"' EXIT
trap 'exit 143' TERM
trap 'exit 130' INT

"$@"

instruction:
Write `csv_to_env.sh` (bash): `csv_to_env.sh FILE.csv` converts a two-column CSV (`key,value`, first line is a header) into shell-safe export lines `export KEY='value'` on stdout.
Rules: skip the header, blank lines and lines starting with `#`; the key is everything before the FIRST comma and must match `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`; the value is everything after it (it may contain commas, spaces, `=`) and is single-quoted
with embedded single quotes escaped as `'\''`; tolerate CRLF line endings; a last line without trailing newline still counts. Invalid lines (bad key or no comma) are reported as `invalid line: <line>` on stderr, skipped, and make the final exit code 1.
Unreadable/missing file or no argument: exit 2. Shellcheck-clean.

reference.csv_to_env.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

[ $# -eq 1 ] && [ -r "$1" ] || { echo "usage: $0 FILE.csv" >&2; exit 2; }

first=1
rc=0
while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
  line=${line%$'\r'}
  if [ "$first" -eq 1 ]; then
    first=0
    continue
  fi
  case $line in
    '' | '#'*) continue ;;
  esac
  key=${line%%,*}
  value=${line#*,}
  if [ "$key" = "$line" ] || [[ ! $key =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]]; then
    echo "invalid line: $line" >&2
    rc=1
    continue
  fi
  value=${value//\'/\'\\\'\'}
  printf "export %s='%s'\n" "$key" "$value"
done < "$1"
exit "$rc"

`fetch_token.sh` logs in to an API with HTTP basic auth but leaks the password everywhere: it takes it as a command-line argument (visible in `ps` and shell history), echoes it, and runs with `set -x` (traces credentials), and passes it in curl's argv.
Fix it: the password comes ONLY from the environment variable `API_PASS` (exit 2 with a message that does not contain the value if it is unset/empty); the user is `deploy`; no `set -x`, no echoing the secret; curl must receive the credentials via a config on stdin
(`curl -K -` / `--config -`, e.g. `printf 'user = "%s:%s"\n' ... | curl -K - ...`), never in its argument list. Keep requesting `https://api.example.com/v1/token` and saving to `token.json`. Neither stdout, stderr nor curl's argv may contain the secret. Shellcheck-clean.

files.fetch_token.sh:
#!/bin/bash
set -x
API_USER=deploy
API_PASS=$1
echo "Logging in with password $API_PASS"
curl -u "$API_USER:$API_PASS" https://api.example.com/v1/token -o token.json
echo "token saved"

reference.fetch_token.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

if [ -z "${API_PASS:-}" ]; then
  echo "API_PASS is not set" >&2
  exit 2
fi
api_user=deploy

printf 'user = "%s:%s"\n' "$api_user" "$API_PASS" |
  curl --silent --show-error --fail -K - -o token.json https://api.example.com/v1/token
echo "token saved"

instruction:
`install.sh URL SHA256 PREFIX` installs a CLI binary, but today it pipes a remote script into bash with root rights and trusts whatever it gets. Harden it: download the file with `curl --fail ... -o <temp file>` (temp file via `mktemp`, always removed),
verify the SHA-256 against the argument using `sha256sum -c` BEFORE installing (mismatch: print `checksum mismatch` to stderr, exit 1, install nothing), then install it as `PREFIX/bin/tool` with mode 0755 (create dirs as needed; use `install -D -m 0755`).
Wrong usage: exit 2. Strict mode on. The expected hash is a 64-hex string; reject anything else with exit 2. Shellcheck-clean.

files.install.sh:
#!/bin/bash
URL=$1
curl -sL $URL | sudo bash
cp /tmp/tool $3/bin/tool
chmod 777 $3/bin/tool

reference.install.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

[ $# -eq 3 ] || { echo "usage: $0 URL SHA256 PREFIX" >&2; exit 2; }
url=$1
sha=$2
prefix=$3
[[ $sha =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$ ]] || { echo "SHA256 must be 64 hex characters" >&2; exit 2; }

tmp=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT

curl --fail --silent --show-error --location -o "$tmp" "$url"
if ! echo "$sha  $tmp" | sha256sum -c --status -; then
  echo "checksum mismatch" >&2
  exit 1
fi
install -D -m 0755 "$tmp" "$prefix/bin/tool"
echo "installed $prefix/bin/tool"

instruction:
`run_job.sh NAME` runs `jobs/NAME.sh` for an operator-facing web hook, but NAME flows into `eval`, so `backup; touch pwned` executes arbitrary commands. Harden it: validate NAME against `^[a-z0-9_-]+$` (else print `invalid job name` to stderr and exit 2 WITHOUT running anything),
no `eval`/`bash -c` with interpolated input, run the job with `bash "jobs/$name.sh"` (no exec bit needed), and exit 1 with `unknown job: NAME` when `jobs/NAME.sh` does not exist. Exactly one argument required (else exit 2). Shellcheck-clean.

reference.run_job.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

[ $# -eq 1 ] || { echo "usage: $0 NAME" >&2; exit 2; }
name=$1
if [[ ! $name =~ ^[a-z0-9_-]+$ ]]; then
  echo "invalid job name" >&2
  exit 2
fi
if [ ! -f "jobs/$name.sh" ]; then
  echo "unknown job: $name" >&2
  exit 1
fi
bash "jobs/$name.sh"

	kubectl diff -n $(ENV) -f k8s/

instruction:
This Makefile mis-handles shell vs make syntax. Problems: `$HOME` and `$(date +%s)`-style shell expansions are eaten by make (needs `$$`), each recipe line runs in its own shell so the `cd` has no effect on the next line,
and the build number is recomputed lazily every time it is referenced (`=` instead of `:=`). Fix: `BUILD := $(shell date +%s)` evaluated once, the `cd sub` and `make` joined into one shell command (`cd sub && $(MAKE)`), and the shell variables escaped
(`$$HOME`, `$$(...)`). Targets `info` and `sub` stay phony.

files.Makefile:
BUILD = $(shell date +%s)

.PHONY: info sub

info:
	@echo "home=$HOME build=$(BUILD) user=$(id -un)"

sub:
	cd sub
	$(MAKE)

reference.Makefile:
BUILD := $(shell date +%s)

.PHONY: info sub

info:
	@echo "home=$$HOME build=$(BUILD) user=$$(id -un)"

sub:
	cd sub && $(MAKE)

cd on its own recipe line

instruction:
`make` recompiles everything every time and ignores header changes. Fix the Makefile to be incremental: `app` must depend on the object files and link them (use `$@` / `$^`), a pattern rule `%.o: %.c` compiles with `$<`/`$@`
(and objects depend on `util.h`), file targets (`app`, objects) must NOT be declared phony, and only `all`, `clean` remain phony. Keep `CC ?= cc`, `CFLAGS ?= -O2 -Wall`. Default goal: `all`, which builds `app`.

files.Makefile:
CC ?= cc
CFLAGS ?= -O2 -Wall

.PHONY: all app main.o util.o clean

all: app

app:
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c main.c -o main.o
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c util.c -o util.o
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o app main.o util.o

clean:
	rm -f app main.o util.o

reference.Makefile:
CC ?= cc
CFLAGS ?= -O2 -Wall
OBJS := main.o util.o

.PHONY: all clean

all: app

app: $(OBJS)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^

%.o: %.c util.h
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

clean:
	rm -f app $(OBJS)

warn about undefined variables (`MAKEFLAGS += --warn-undefined-variables`) and drop the `-` prefixes that ignore errors on important commands (keep the `-` only on `rm -f` cleanup if you like - `rm -f` already ignores missing files, so it is not needed).
Targets and commands stay: `report.txt` is produced by `sort data.txt | uniq -c > report.txt`; `all: report.txt`; `clean` removes it.

all: report.txt

report.txt: data.txt
	-sort data.txt | uniq -c > report.txt

	-rm -f report.txt

.SHELLFLAGS := -eu -o pipefail -c
MAKEFLAGS += --warn-undefined-variables

.PHONY: all clean

all: report.txt

report.txt: data.txt
	sort data.txt | uniq -c > report.txt

clean:
	rm -f report.txt

and `aws_iam_policy.reports` using `policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.reports.json`. No `*` actions and no bare `*` resources.

These instances use `count` over a list, so removing a server from the middle of the list destroys and recreates every later server. Convert to `for_each` over a map keyed by server name, preserving behaviour:
`variable "servers"` becomes `map(object({ type = string }))` (no default) and the resource uses `for_each = var.servers`, `instance_type = each.value.type`, `tags = { Name = each.key }`, `ami = var.ami_id`.

Terraform reasoning. Current state was created from `servers = ["a", "b", "c"]` with
```
resource "aws_instance" "web" {
  count         = length(var.servers)
  ami           = var.ami
  instance_type = "t3.micro"
  tags          = { Name = var.servers[count.index] }
}
```
so the state holds `aws_instance.web[0]` (Name=a), `[1]` (Name=b), `[2]` (Name=c). The list is changed to `["a", "c"]` (b removed) and `terraform apply` is run.

`"safer_alternative"` (one of the strings `"for_each"` or `"count"`: the meta-argument that would have destroyed ONLY the instance for `b`). Only addresses of the form `aws_instance.web[<index>]`, sorted ascending.
